text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automated page fired: PagerDuty rule 'network-lb-target-health' -> pd_incident_98321. Symptoms: ALB target health degraded + TLS handshake spikes in us-west-2; DNS propagation showing mixed A records from edge. Auto-escalation threshold reached (2mins).

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident pd_incident_98321 created and sent to: @lee.sre (primary oncall). Escalation in 5m to @maria.ops if not acknowledged.

lee.sre: ack'd. On it. initial check: seeing ~28% unhealthy targets on alb-prod-usw2, most failing with TLS handshake 40ms->fail. Also getting intermittent NXDOMAIN hits from one edge POP. Not a full outage yet but customer error rate up ~6% for generation requests.

alex.neteng: seeing a flurry of DNS TTLs (some zones with 300s, others 3600s). Route53 change from this morning may not have fully propagated to some ISPs. Also, some ALB IPs are returning older certs at certain edge locations.

lee.sre: timeline look: around 2125590900 we rolled a small cert refresh to ALB (staged). Most regions OK, but us-west-2 started showing increased TLS failures right after that. Could be cert edge push + stale DNS mapping -> clients hitting old cert IPs.

maria.ops: looping in @sam-platform for rollback orchestration and @alex.neteng for DNS status. Sam can we pause cert rollout or revert? If we revert ALB cert, might break clients already on new cert.

sam-platform: I can pause further rollout. Revert is possible but will take ~7-10m and risk flapping. Recommend targeted failover: shift traffic from problematic ALB target group to healthy pool in us-west-1 while we sort cert/dns.

lee.sre: agree with failover. Initiating weighted routing change -> reduce weight on ALB-usw2 to 10% and increase ALB-usw1 to 90% via traffic-router (canary style). Command:

```
traffic-router set-weight --env prod --origin ALB-usw2 --weight 10
traffic-router set-weight --env prod --origin ALB-usw1 --weight 90
```

oncall-bot: ops action recorded: traffic-router change initiated by lee.sre. Change id: tr-2125591-42. Rollback window 15m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident pd_incident_98321 acknowledged by lee.sre. Escalation suppressed.

alex.neteng: dig checks:
```
> dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai A
54.213.12.99
3.236.45.22
# but some resolvers return 3.236.45.22 only -> hitting older edge pool with expired cert
```

maria.ops: customer impact assessment: ~6% error rate for customers in us-west across generation endpoints, embeddings unaffected. No confirmed data exfiltration. A small set of enterprise customers using pinned IPs may see failures.

sam-platform: traffic weights applied successfully. Observability: error rate dropping to ~2% in the last 3m for us-west region. Latency stable. Rolling forward with DNS check.

lee.sre: starting targeted ALB target recycle in usw2 for hosts showing TLS failures; will also re-deploy cert to edge with force flag to ensure new cert available. Steps:
- `aws elbv2 deregister-targets` small batch
- redeploy cert to edge CDN

alex.neteng: I'm running a Route53 health check sweep and forcing lower TTL on the zone for api.redwood.ai to 60s to speed fallback. Command:
```
route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://lower-ttl.json
```

maria.ops: alerting support rotations: emailing customers-party@redwood to inform of partial impact and that mitigation is in progress. Draft note: "We identified a transient TLS handshake issue affecting a subset of requests in us-west. We've applied traffic routing mitigations; root cause appears related to cert rollout + stale DNS mappings. Investigating and will follow up." Agree?

lee.sre: yes send that. Add: guidance to retry requests; embed link to status page.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Scheduled escalation to @maria.ops canceled by acknowledgement.

oncall-bot: monitoring: error-rate/us-west dropped from 6.2% -> 1.8% since traffic weight change. CPU on ALB-usw2 targets normal. TLS handshake failures count falling.

sam-platform: recommending leaving weights for 20m to confirm stability, then gradually restore to default. Also suggest post-incident: update our rollout playbook to include DNS TTL checks pre-cert-rollout.

lee.sre: agree. I'll take ownership of the postmortem and include reproductions: cert rollout -> edge push lag -> resolver cache mismatch. Action items: 1) add preflight TTL scan; 2) add cert push verification across POPs; 3) add automated rollback if TLS failures spike >5% in 5m.

maria.ops: handing to me for next shift. @lee.sre please post a short incident summary before handoff. I'll open the incident channel for follow-ups and timeline reconstruction.

lee.sre: summary: pd_incident_98321: automated page for ALB target health + TLS handshake spikes in us-west 2. Mitigation: traffic weight re-route to us-west-1, targeted target recycle, forced cert redeploy, TTL lowered to 60s to accelerate DNS convergence. Customer impact: ~6% error increase localized to us-west; enterprise pinned IPs may have seen failures. Current status: stable, monitoring. Handoff to maria.ops.

maria.ops: acknowledged handoff. I'll coordinate the write-up and postmortem. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
